column1: Notice that this consumption function exhibits the three properties that Keynes posited. It satisfies Keynes’s first property because the marginal propensity to consume c is between zero and one, so that higher income leads to higher consumption and also to higher saving. This consumption function satisfies Keynes’s second property because the average propensity to consume APC is APC 5 C/Y 5 C – /Y  c. As Y rises, C – /Y falls, and so the average propensity to consume C/Y falls. And finally, this consumption function satisfies Keynes’s third property because the interest rate is not included in this equation as a determinant of consumption.
